is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles maculipennis s.s. collected in Iran (page 1, title and Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The authors screened the GSTe2 gene in An. maculipennis for mutations (mentioning I114T, L119F, F120L), but found none of the target markers; they only reported a novel N148D substitution (page 1 Abstract; page 7: 'Well-known GSTe2 mutation (I114T, L119F, and F120L) were not detected in An. maculepennis species'). Furthermore, target marker GSTe2 L119F is specific to An. funestus.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No target resistance markers were detected or genotyped; only sequence analysis of non-target/novel mutations in GSTe2 was reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from West Azarbaijan and Zanjan provinces in Iran, which is not an African country (page 2, Section 2.1 Study site and Table 1).

is_primary_study.evidence: The study is a primary empirical field collection and sequencing investigation (page 2, Section 2).

sub_country_location.evidence: Sampling sites are listed at the village/town level: Nazloo, Jarchiloo, Kooraneh, Larijan, and Gharabooteh (page 2, Table 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted 'during different collections from 2015 to 2018' (4-year window) and not resolved to finer collection dates per sample (page 2, Section 2.1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Routine primary collection of Anopheles maculipennis in Iran.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary data is needed since the study fails eligibility on geographic and target marker criteria.

assessment.summary: This study sequenced the GSTe2 gene of Anopheles maculipennis s.s. collected in Iran between 2015 and 2018. It found a novel N148D variant in 19 sequenced specimens, but did not study African populations nor detect any canonical target resistance markers.
exclusion_reasons: Mosquitoes were collected in Iran, not an African country.
Does not genotype or report any of the eligible target resistance markers in African malaria vectors.
